title: Formal gluing of finite commutative algebras
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $t\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_t\in R$, and put $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$. Suppose the induced map $R/K\to S/KS$ is an isomorphism. Let $E^{\prime}$ be a commutative $S$-algebra and, for each $i$, let $E_i$ be a commutative $R_{f_i}$-algebra. Suppose there are algebra isomorphisms $\alpha_i:(E^{\prime})_{f_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_i\otimes_R S$ over $S_{f_i}$ and $\alpha_{ij}:(E_i)_{f_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}(E_j)_{f_i}$ over $R_{f_if_j}$, whose underlying modules and maps form an object of $\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. If $E^{\prime}$ is finitely generated as an $S$-module and every $E_i$ is finitely generated as an $R_{f_i}$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], then there exists a commutative $R$-algebra $D$, finitely generated as an $R$-module, with algebra isomorphisms $D\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}E^{\prime}$ and $D_{f_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_i$ which together give an isomorphism from the canonical gluing datum of $D$ to the specified datum. In particular these algebra isomorphisms commute with all the $\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_{ij}$.

source.place: Tags 05ER (proposition-equivalence) and 05EU (remark-formal-glueing-algebras), including the tensor-structure and algebra-category assertion in the final two sentences of 05EU

proof.text: Forget multiplication in the specified algebra datum and call the resulting module datum $\mathbf E$. By hypothesis it is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$. Apply the essential-surjectivity clause of [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence](2), with $I=K$: its flatness and quotient-isomorphism hypotheses are exactly ours. Obtain an $R$-module $M$ and an isomorphism $a:\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathbf E$. Write its component module isomorphisms as $a':M\otimes_RS\to E'$ and $a_i:M_{f_i}\to E_i$. Both $a$ and its inverse satisfy the morphism compatibility equations of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. No multiplication on $M$ is assumed.

Define $D$ to be the subset of $E'\times\prod_iE_i$ consisting of tuples $d=(e',(e_i)_i)$ with $\alpha_i(e'/1)=e_i\otimes1$ for every $i$ and $\alpha_{ij}(e_i/1)=e_j/1$ for every $i,j$. Its underlying $R$-module is exactly $H^0$ of the underlying module datum $\mathbf E$ of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0] (same tuples, same equations). Give it coordinatewise addition and multiplication. Each equality is an equality of two ring-homomorphism images, so it is preserved by sums, negatives, products and the unit. The tuple of the images of any $r\in R$ also satisfies every equality, since all transition maps are algebra maps. Thus $D$ is a commutative unital $R$-algebra, with $R$-algebra projections $p':D\to E'$ and $p_i:D\to E_i$. This is an actual subring construction, not a choice of an unknown algebra structure.

source.place: Tag 05EU (remark-formal-glueing-algebras), final two sentences, expanded by the matching-tuples construction of Tag 05EL

proof.text: Define the $R$-linear map $\lambda:M\to D$ by $m\mapsto(a'(m\otimes1),(a_i(m/1))_i)$. It lands in $D$ by the compatibility equations for $a$. On the whole product of modules, the componentwise isomorphism $(a',(a_i)_i)$ carries a tuple satisfying the canonical matching equations to a tuple satisfying the displayed equations defining $D$, and its inverse does the reverse, by the morphism equations for $a^{-1}$. For the canonical datum those matching tuples are precisely $\ker\beta$ in [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-complex-exact]: the canonical comparison identifies $(M\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$ with $M_{f_i}\otimes_RS$ and the double localizations with $M_{f_if_j}$. That lemma, with the same $R,S,f_i,K$, says $m\mapsto(m\otimes1,(m/1)_i)$ is injective and has image exactly $\ker\beta$. It follows that $\lambda$ is bijective.

source.place: Tags 05EL (remark-glueing-data), 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data), and 05ER: identify the matching-tuples module with any algebraizing module

proof.text: Define $q':D\otimes_RS\to E'$ on pure tensors by $q'(d\otimes s)=p'(d)s$, and $q_i:D_{f_i}\to E_i$ by $q_i(d/f_i^n)=p_i(d)/f_i^n$. The first formula is balanced and additive, hence defines the tensor map; it preserves multiplication since $(p'(d)s)(p'(e)u)=p'(de)su$, and it sends $1\otimes1$ to $1$. The localization formula is well-defined by the fraction relation, since $f_i$ is invertible in $E_i$; it preserves sums, products and the unit by the fraction formulas. Thus these are respectively $S$- and $R_{f_i}$-algebra maps. On pure tensors and fractions one has $q'\circ(\lambda\otimes_RS)=a'$ and $q_i\circ\lambda_{f_i}=a_i$: both sides send $m\otimes s$ to $s\,a'(m\otimes1)$, respectively $m/f_i^n$ to $f_i^{-n}a_i(m/1)$. Extension of scalars and localization preserve the isomorphism $\lambda$, as applying the same operations to $\lambda^{-1}$ gives inverse maps. Hence $q'$ and all $q_i$ are bijective. Their inverses preserve the algebra operations by injectivity, so they are algebra isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 05EU, tensor-structure and algebra-category assertion: projection maps and their bijectivity explicitly checked

proof.text:
These isomorphisms respect the prescribed gluing maps. For $d\in D$, $s\in S$ and $n\ge0$, the prime-chart square evaluated at $(d\otimes s)/f_i^n$ asserts
$\alpha_i(p'(d)s/f_i^n)=(p_i(d)/f_i^n)\otimes s$.
This follows from $\alpha_i(p'(d)/1)=p_i(d)\otimes1$ and $S_{f_i}$-linearity. For $d\in D$ and $a,b\ge0$, the chart-chart square evaluated at $(d/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ asserts
$\alpha_{ij}((p_i(d)/f_i^a)/f_j^b)=(p_j(d)/f_j^b)/f_i^a$.
This is $\alpha_{ij}(p_i(d)/1)=p_j(d)/1$ multiplied by the inverses of $f_i^af_j^b$ in the common localization. Fractions and sums of pure tensors generate the relevant modules, so the squares commute on every element. Thus $(q',(q_i)_i)$ is an isomorphism from the canonical gluing datum of $D$ to the specified one, with algebra maps on every component.

source.place: Tags 05EL and 05EU: explicit compatibility with both sorts of transition isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-finite-modules] to the underlying $R$-module of $D$, with $I=K$. Flatness and the quotient isomorphism have not changed. Its base change and localizations are identified by $q'$ and $q_i$ with the finite modules $E'$ and $E_i$ in the hypotheses. Finite generation is preserved by these module isomorphisms: inverse images of a finite generating family generate. The reverse implication of the cited criterion therefore makes $D$ finitely generated over $R$. Together with the constructed algebra isomorphisms and the checked squares, this proves every clause.

proof_origin.place: Explicit matching-subring argument expanding Tags 05EU and 05EL, using the module equivalence 05ER and exactness 05EK; no abstract monoidal-equivalence theorem is assumed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_algebra_of_formalGlueing {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R) (hflat : (algebraMap R S).Flat) (hquot : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) (E' : Type w) [CommRing E'] [Algebra S E'] [Algebra R E'] [IsScalarTower R S E'] (E : Fin t → Type w) [∀ i, CommRing (E i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (E i)] [∀ i, Algebra (Localization.Away (f i)) (E i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away (f i)) (E i)] (alpha : ∀ i : Fin t, LocalizedModule.Away (f i) E' ≃ₐ[R] (S ⊗[R] E i)) (alphaOverlap : ∀ i j : Fin t, LocalizedModule.Away (f j) (E i) ≃ₐ[R] LocalizedModule.Away (f i) (E j)) (hdata : ∃ X : Data.{u, v, w} (algebraMap R S) f, X.M' = ModuleCat.of S E' ∧ (∀ i : Fin t, X.M i = ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (E i)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin t, HEq (X.alpha i).toLinearMap (alpha i).toLinearMap) ∧ (∀ i j : Fin t, HEq (X.alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (alphaOverlap i j).toLinearMap)) (hfinitePrime : Module.Finite S E') (hfiniteChart : ∀ i : Fin t, Module.Finite (Localization.Away (f i)) (E i)) : ∃ (D : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing D) (_ : Algebra R D), Module.Finite R D ∧ ∃ (a' : (S ⊗[R] D) ≃ₐ[S] E') (a : ∀ i : Fin t, LocalizedModule.Away (f i) D ≃ₐ[R] E i), (∀ (i : Fin t) (d : D), alpha i (LocalizedModule.mk (a' (1 ⊗ₜ[R] d)) 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] a i (LocalizedModule.mk d 1)) ∧ (∀ (i j : Fin t) (d : D), alphaOverlap i j (LocalizedModule.mk (a i (LocalizedModule.mk d 1)) 1) = LocalizedModule.mk (a j (LocalizedModule.mk d 1)) 1)
lean.note: The map R → S is encoded by Algebra R S.
